Archie vs Zapier, Make and n8n.

Automation tools are very good at the things you can describe as a rule. The interesting question is what happens to the jobs you cannot.

Archie is in testing. The waitlist hears the day it opens. See where it stands → Checked against the sources below on August 19, 2026.

The short answer

One you build. The other you tell.

An automation is a diagram: this trigger, then that step, then this condition, and it does exactly that every time. An agent is told the job in a sentence and works out the steps, which is more useful when the input varies and less predictable when it does not.

Where an agent wins

Four things a diagram cannot do.

A diagram does exactly what it says. These are the jobs that never fit in one.

You say the job; Archie finds the steps

“Reply to everyone who asked about pricing this week” is one sentence to an agent and a week of boxes to a diagram, and the case nobody drew is the one it handles.

Archie writes in your words

A reply drafted, a list kept up, a report written, with your own way of writing to go by.

Nothing sends without you

A draft waits for your send, a calendar change waits for your yes, and neither is a settingSource 5.

One reply, AI included, on your own account

$0.01 to $0.11 for a reply from a fully loaded agent, at the AI company’s price, with a cap you set. The app is $30 a monthSource 4.

Side by side

Where the two approaches part company.

Archie compared with automation tools, across how work is described, where it runs, where credentials live, and what it costs
  Archie Zapier, Make, n8n

When the input isn’t what you expected It reads it and decides, then shows you The step does what it was built to do

Prices read from each company’s own pricing page on August 19, 2026, and listed in full at the foot of this page. n8n prices in euros, so that figure is left in euros: a converted price is not a checked one.

Where automation tools win

Four reasons to keep using automation tools.

If your work is already automated and it works, keep it.

Automation tools run without your computer

Cloud automation keeps going with your computer off and your laptop shut. Archie needs a computer that stays awake, and that is a genuine limitation rather than a design flourish.

Automation tools do the same thing every time

A rule is auditable and repeatable. For invoicing, compliance, or anything where a surprise is expensive, predictable beats clever.

Years of connectors

These are mature catalogues covering far more services than Archie does, built up over a long time.

Built for teams

Shared workspaces, run histories and roles are what these tools are for. Archie runs a personal agent on one person’s computer.

Worth saying

Archie and automation tools sit happily side by side.

Automations are good at the plumbing between systems. An agent is good at the part where somebody has to read something and decide. Plenty of people will want the rule to keep firing and the agent to handle what the rule cannot describe.

Sources for every figure and claim on this page
1Zapier, from $29.99 a month

Read from zapier.com/pricing on August 19, 2026: a free tier of 100 tasks a month, and Professional from $29.99 a month at 750 tasks, or $19.99 billed annually.

2Make, from $12 a month

Read from make.com/en/pricing on August 19, 2026: a free tier of up to 1,000 credits a month, Core at $12 a month and Pro at $21, each quoted at 10,000 credits.

3n8n, from 20€ a month

Read from n8n.io/pricing on August 19, 2026: Starter at 20€ a month billed annually and Pro at 50€, plus a self-hostable Community edition published on GitHub under their Fair-code license.

4Archie, $30 a month

Our own price, with the AI usage that sits on top of it broken down on the pricing page.

5Nothing sends without you

Email and calendar changes are drafted and held for approval in the app. The mechanism, and the honest limit on it, are on the Trust page.

6Where your account credentials sit

Archie keeps the tokens for your connected accounts in your computer’s own password store. What that means, and every outbound connection it makes, are on the Trust page.

What we have not claimed

Nothing on this page says any of these tools cannot do something. All three have AI features and all three are still changing. The contrast drawn here is between describing work as steps and describing it in a sentence, which is a difference in approach, not a scorecard.
